messages:
incident-bot: PAGER SEV2 -> multi-GPU collective (NCCL) timeouts on prod-infer-2 cluster. job=job-8432, tp4 pipeline. alert: https://alerts.redwood/ALERT-8432 :rotating_light:

sre-alex: grabbing logs now, looks like repeated NCCL TIMEOUT + CUDA Xid79 around 11:32:12 UTC. I'll post excerpts.

ml-runtime-maya: fwiw we've seen KV-cache churn for this topology under long contexts before. eviction burst at ~11:32:10 might align.

sre-alex: logs: ```
[2026-03-15T11:32:11Z] ncclCommAbort on rank 3: NCCL TIMEOUT waiting at allreduce.cpp:211
[2026-03-15T11:32:12Z] driver: Xid 79, GPU hang detected, process 12984 (python)
[2026-03-15T11:32:12Z] nv_peer_error: channel 2 timeout, retry 0
```

oncall-ryan: taking the pager. initial hypothesis: GPU hang on node prod-gpu-21 caused NCCL to stall the TP pipeline, downstream jobs saw repeated communicator resets.

eng-jordan: can you confirm affected pods? `kubectl get pods -n inference -l job=job-8432 -o wide` shows pods spread across prod-gpu-21, prod-gpu-22.

infra-kim: node metrics: GPU1 on prod-gpu-21 shows +10s stall on heartbeat, dmesg shows repeated Xid79 + nvlink warnings. Memory usage not maxed but sustained high GPU memory and KV-cache eviction.

sre-alex: mitigation plan: 1) cordon prod-gpu-21, 2) drain affected pods (allow jobs to failover to same pool), 3) restart container runtime on prod-gpu-21 if node still flapping, 4) apply temporary model-fallback to quantized variant for in-flight requests to reduce KV pressure. executing steps now.

oncall-ryan: cordoning node -> `kubectl cordon prod-gpu-21` :white_check_mark:

oncall-ryan: draining job pods -> `kubectl drain prod-gpu-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (jobs will get rescheduled to prod-gpu-22/23).

ml-runtime-maya: enabling fallback routing for job-8432 to model:redwood-7b-q4f fallback profile to reduce per-GPU memory. route change pushed to routing service.

customer-success-liz: customer impact: small fraction of hosted embeddings requests returned 502/timeout (~0.4% of traffic) between 11:32-11:40 UTC. Affected customers: Beta partners (AcmeSearch) — notifying them now.

eng-jordan: after drain, multiple pods rescheduled successfully to prod-gpu-22. observed reduced NCCL timeouts. continuing to monitor.

infra-kim: restarted container runtime (nvidia-containerd) on prod-gpu-21 as a precaution: `systemctl restart nvidia-containerd` — checking kernel logs.

sre-alex: kernel logs post-restart: ```
Mar 15 11:34:05 prod-gpu-21 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 15 11:34:06 prod-gpu-21 kernel: nv_peer_error: link reset detected on GPU1
```

oncall-ryan: marking node unschedulable until vendor patch verification. Patching ticket created: INFRA-5429.

eng-jordan: rolling back fallback now that workload moved and timeouts subsided. Keeping fallback policy in console for 30m as safety.

ml-runtime-maya: KV-cache metrics show eviction rate dropped from 4800 evictions/min to 120 evictions/min after fallback. Suggests memory pressure was a trigger.

sre-alex: verdict: primary failure mode = GPU hang (Xid79) on prod-gpu-21 causing NCCL communicator stall; contributing factor = KV-cache thrash under long context TP workload.

customer-success-liz: sent interim customer note to affected partners: short summary + ETA for RCA.

oncall-ryan: closing pager as mitigated. will hand off to infra for postmortem and potential firmware/driver upgrades. tagging eng/runtime, infra, and ml-runtime teams.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated in 18 minutes. Creating incident record and assigned postmortem INF-2026-03-15-8432. :memo:
